question: Is the "Platform Reliability (Ground Control)" team's investment mix shift a genuine, approved finding, or is the comparison baseline missing?

invariants.assert: A named subject mention that misses its intended target never silently widens to org-wide/broader scope; widening is only ever a disclosed, terminal answered_with_gaps/needs_clarification outcome.
invariants.$comment: check=no_internal_error is a real, always-meaningful floor (the run must not crash to internal_error) but is NARROWER than this invariant's full 'assert' claim above -- Lane 2a's invariants.py registry (read directly, 2026-08-06) has no checker yet for the specific widening/unauthorized-candidate/persistence claim this category names. Tracked as a Lane 2a checker gap, not silently claimed as fully enforced.

invariants.assert: A rule/finding whose computation genuinely lacks a comparison baseline or attribution denominator (missing_attribution / insufficient sample-coverage-cohort) is reported as a disclosed gap, never silently presented as a confidently-computed, approved finding. This is the same disclosure discipline inv.no-silent-widening polices for subject scope, generalized here from geographic/org scope to statistical confidence -- reporting an un-attributable investment-ratio shift with full confidence would be exactly the silent-widening failure mode this invariant exists to catch, just applied to a denominator instead of a subject.
invariants.$comment: check=no_internal_error is a real, always-meaningful floor (the run must not crash to internal_error) but is NARROWER than this invariant's full 'assert' claim above -- Lane 2a's invariants.py registry (read directly, 2026-08-06) has no checker for the specific fabrication-prevention claim this ad-hoc category names. Tracked as a Lane 2a checker gap, not silently claimed as fully enforced.

invariants.assert: The run's derived wave4_case_result.v1 resolution_path equals this case's resolution-profiles/deterministic-v1.json entry's own resolution_path (null is a valid, asserted value for n/a-subject cases that never attempt mention resolution).

notes: General/non-workload instance of an 'unknown denominator' condition, distinct from workload.team.without-denominator's workload-specific instance: grounded in dimension_observation_adapters.py, checked directly -- ALL FOUR of that module's dimension-observation adapters (including investment_allocation_shift_observation, category 8/investment_balance's only bound HEALTH_RULE_REGISTRY rule) report attribution_present=False unconditionally (CHAOS-3331, module docstring confirms this explicitly). operational_deficiency_service.py's own docstring independently confirms the downstream consequence: 'a genuinely computed shift therefore lands in suppressed_findings with missing_attribution, never a launch finding, until CHAOS-3331 lands.' This is a genuine, always-true production behavior today (not fixture-dependent, unlike most of this corpus's positive/negative controls) -- true for ANY team subject, not just this one, because attribution_present=False is hardcoded, not computed per-fixture. Same quoted-full-label EXACT-resolution mechanism as workload.team.with-denominator/deficiency.team.applicable-rule (see those cases' notes for the live-verified reason the bare 'Ground Control' alias mention is not used) -- resolution_path=deterministic-exact, expected_scope_resolution_outcome=exact per those already-established resolution-profiles/deterministic-v1.json precedents for this exact subject/mention shape. expected_public_outcome=answered_with_gaps follows the SAME settled-by-code fact those cases' resolution-profile entries already document (terminal_frames.wrap_legacy_answer_as_frame: a real DevAnswer terminal on today's deterministic/legacy stack always maps to PublicOutcome.ANSWERED_WITH_GAPS, never plain ANSWERED, because the legacy model-tool-choice loop never computes a DevCompletionBlock).
